prompts.text: Why do you want to attend UMass Amherst?
Why did you choose the major you did?

Commonwealth Honors College is a community in which students examine complex questions, learn across differences, and connect their academic interests to the world around them. What is one perspective, experience, or question you would bring to this community, and how would you hope to develop it at UMass Amherst?
prompts.applies_to: Applicants interested in joining Commonwealth Honors College

prompts.text: At UMass Amherst, no two students are alike. Our communities and groups often define us and shape our individual worlds. Community can refer to various aspects, including shared geography, religion, race/ethnicity, income, ideology, and more. Please choose one of your communities or groups and describe its significance. Explain how, as a product of this community or group, you would enrich our campus.
prompts.applies_to: Applicants not interested in Commonwealth Honors College

notes: Three required UMass-specific short answers: prompts 1 and 2 for everyone, plus ONE of prompts 3/4. The official admissions page says 'The third question depends on whether or not you're interested in joining Commonwealth Honors College' (Honors-interested -> prompt 3; others -> prompt 4); the official FY27 (2026-2027) UREP essay handout says 'Please answer one of the following questions' - modeled as choose 1 of 2. Cycle confirmed as 2026-27 via the official FY27 handout (uploaded 2026-09, titled for the '2026-2027 Common App questions'), whose prompts match the admissions page. Text is copied from the official first-year application instructions page, which states no word limits; the 100-word limit comes from the official FY27 handout ('UMASS CUSTOM QUESTIONS (100 WORDS EACH)'). Minor wording variants exist: the FY27 handout phrases prompt 2 as 'Why did you choose this major(s)?'; third-party sites (Esslo, CollegeVine 2025-26) quote the Common App wording as 'Please tell us why you want to attend UMass Amherst.' and 'Please tell us why you chose the Major(s) you did.' and Esslo gives the honors prompt ending '...develop it at UMass?'. The exact in-app Common App wording could not be viewed (login required). The Commonwealth Honors College essay page (honorspaths.honors.umass.edu) returned HTTP 503.
